evidence.ranking_order: semantic acceptance, exact role cells, exact semantic verdicts, stable cases, fewest regressions, cells at or above the confidence reference, then minimum, p10, median and mean confidence, fewest question bytes, bundle id

data.explanation: 32 role-complete bundles (baseline included) x 14 frozen oracle cases x 2 repeats: 896 calls, 0 retries. Bundle r-sig-list.a-one-source.c-cur is the top-ranked semantically accepted set: 84/84 role cells, 28/28 threshold-0 verdicts, 14/14 stable cases, zero regressions against the baseline. Confidence is diagnostic only; production review keeps the 0.6 threshold. Tuner note: the baseline (current questions) scored 82/84 role cells and 13/14 cases; it answered relevant=yes (0.91, 0.88) on topical-read-records, an item that only reads records, so it would pass a not-applicable item as satisfied. The sealed set's lowest cell is relevant=yes at 0.61 on fixture-pass (the fixture names no edit verb), just above the 0.6 production threshold; production near-threshold re-asks apply.

criteria.no: The item does none of these: it is silent on where shared rules live, describes only a tool's own behaviour, rewords text without moving or removing a restatement, restates a shared rule, or is about something else.
criteria.unclear: The item touches shared rules and derivative tool records, but whether it makes them single-sourced in sc-agent cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item makes a derivative tool's record defer to sc-agent for a shared rule, removes a restated shared rule from such a record, or consolidates a shared rule in sc-agent's records.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state, plan or carry out that a rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, model resolution and the like) is specified only in sc-agent's records, and a derivative tool's records (judge-jev, plan-anchor and others) do not restate it and give only the tool name and the tool's own behaviour? Count it when the item makes a derivative tool's record point to sc-agent for a shared rule instead of stating it, removes a restated shared rule from a derivative tool's record, or moves a shared rule into sc-agent's records. Merely not restating a rule, describing a tool's own behaviour, rewording sc-agent's text, or mentioning records is not stating it.

criteria.no: Doing the described work would not violate the requirement.
criteria.unclear: Whether the described work would violate the requirement cannot be told from the text.
criteria.yes: Doing the described work would violate the requirement.

contradicted.instructions: Would doing what `item.text` describes violate the requirement that a rule that applies to every decidr-based tool is specified only in sc-agent's records; a derivative tool's records do not restate it and give only the tool name and the tool's own behaviour? Violations look like: restating, copying or redefining a shared decidr-tool rule (logging, model resolution and the like) in a derivative tool's records. Omitting the requirement, or describing unrelated work, is not a violation.

criteria.no: The item changes no REQ, NFR or ADR record text: it changes code, tests, dependencies or configuration, fixes a bug, or only reads or mentions records or logging.
criteria.unclear: The item may change record text matching a signal, but the text does not say whether any record text is changed.
criteria.yes: The item adds, edits, moves or rewords text in a record as described by signal (1), (2) or (3).

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` describe work that matches at least one of these signals: (1) it adds or edits a REQ, NFR or ADR record of judge-jev, plan-anchor or another decidr-based tool (for example REQ-JEV-*, or files under docs/requirements/, docs/nfr/, docs/adr/ or docs/<crate>/requirements/); (2) it adds, moves or rewords record text about log placement or log root, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields; (3) it adds or edits an sc-agent record that states a rule for all decidr-based tools. Judge only what the item says it will change. Code changes, tests, bug fixes and reading or reviewing records do not match, even when they mention logging, retries, model resolution or a tool's records.
